source: Mintzberg and Waters (1985) Of strategies, deliberate and emergent
finding: Founding paper. Strategy is a pattern in a stream of actions. Realized strategy = deliberate part + emergent part. Many intended strategies go unrealized. The paper argues the formulation-then-implementation view is seriously limited.
numbers: No sample statistics. Qualitative case studies. Abstract text read via Semantic Scholar API; full text blocked (403).
quote: strategy formation... tended to be treated as an analytic process for establishing long-range goals and action plans
limits: Descriptive, not a test of performance. No test of whether emergent beats deliberate. Publisher page blocked, so only the abstract was read.
agent_relevance: Gives the S9 learning loop a vocabulary: compare intended plan with realized action trace, and keep the emergent part that worked.

source: Wikipedia: Henry Mintzberg
finding: Mintzberg's distinctive claim is that emergent strategy arises informally at any level, as an alternative or complement to deliberate strategy. He calls strategic planning an oxymoron. Key works: The Rise and Fall of Strategic Planning (1994), The Design School (SMJ 1990, 11(3):171-195).
numbers: More than 150 articles, 15 books. No empirical effect sizes.
limits: Secondary encyclopedia source. Describes the theory, not evidence for it.
agent_relevance: Confirms the theory side. Shows the claim is conceptual, so an agent should not treat 'emergent is better' as an empirical finding.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic management
finding: Summarizes Mintzberg: plan vs pattern, emergent when realized pattern differs from intent. 1994 distinction: strategic thinking is synthesis ('connecting the dots'), planning is analysis ('finding the dots'). Strategy can also resist change and exclude signals. Chaffee's adaptive model removes the planning window.
numbers: By 1979 about 45% of Fortune 500 firms used a growth-share matrix variant (adoption, not performance). First 100000 of 211330 characters read.
limits: No planning-performance evidence in the part read. Only half the page read.
agent_relevance: Planning as analysis and synthesis as separate jobs maps to two different agent operators: a code-checked decomposition step and a model-driven synthesis step.

source: Wikipedia: Strategic planning (George, Walker and Monster 2019 meta-analysis)
finding: Meta-analysis by George, Walker and Monster (2019) found strategic planning has a positive effect on organizational performance, especially effectiveness (goal achievement). Having a plan alone is not enough. Benefits depend on formality, comprehensiveness (many options before choosing) and stakeholder management.
numbers: Almost 9,000 public and private organizations. Effect size not given on the page. A 2006 McKinsey survey found many firms had formal planning not used for their most important decisions.
limits: Read only through Wikipedia, not the paper. Mostly public-sector samples, so transfer to firms is uncertain. Effect size not verified.
agent_relevance: Planning helps on average, but process quality (options generated, environment analysis) moderates it. Supports keeping a plan step with breadth requirements.

source: Delmar and Shane (2003) Does business planning facilitate the development of new ventures?
finding: Challenges the view that planning hurts new ventures. Planning is an early precursor to action. It reduces the chance a venture disbands and speeds product development and venture organizing.
numbers: Sample of new Swedish ventures (about 223 per my memory, not verified here). Abstract read via Crossref only.
quote: business planning is an important precursor to action in new ventures
limits: Observational data, not randomized. Survivor bias possible. Full text not opened (publisher blocked). Cited 642 times per Crossref.
agent_relevance: Planning works partly by turning abstract goals into concrete steps. Fits an S-state that converts a goal into checkable subgoals before acting.

source: Brinckmann, Grichnik and Kapsa (2010) Should entrepreneurs plan or just storm the castle? Meta-analysis on contextual factors in the planning-performance relationship in small firms
finding: Meta-analysis of planning vs performance in small firms, testing context moderators (new vs established firms, culture, environment). Title frames the debate as plan vs act. Metadata confirmed; abstract and effect sizes were not readable (publisher blocked, Semantic Scholar abstract elided).
numbers: 520 citations per Crossref. Overall effect reported in the literature as small and positive; exact r and k not verified this session.
limits: Effect sizes not verified. Publisher pages returned 403.
agent_relevance: Planning value depends on context. The agent should vary plan depth by task type rather than always plan or never plan.

source: Planning for the market: business planning before marketing and the continuation of organizing efforts (2004, J. Business Venturing; authors not verified)
finding: Metadata found: 'Planning for the market: business planning before marketing and the continuation of organizing efforts' (cited 344 times). Related literature (not read) argues plans can serve legitimacy, not just decisions.
numbers: No numbers read. Only the title and citation count were retrieved.
limits: Not opened. Listed as a rival explanation: plans may signal legitimacy, not improve decisions.
agent_relevance: A plan can be a performance for a reader, not a thinking aid. Grade the plan by what it changes in action, not by its text.

source: Wikipedia: Lean startup (cited studies)
finding: Page cites no randomized trials. Critics: Felin et al. (2020) say applying lean principles to startups is problematic and gives only incremental outcomes. Contigiani and Levinthal (2019) say its insights were already in organizational-learning theory. Bruneel and Ratinho name three cases where it should not be used: high prototyping cost, testing cost above benefit, teams unable to read experiments. Leatherbee and Katila (2020) report support.
numbers: No sample sizes or effects on the page.
limits: Secondary source. The RCTs on the scientific approach (Camuffo et al. 2020; Koning et al. 2022) were not reachable (publisher 403), so they are not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition for 'act and learn': it fails when tests are costly or results cannot be read. For the agent, cheap code-checked tests favor emergent learning; costly ones favor planning.

source: Wikipedia: Effectuation (Dew et al. 2009; Arend et al. 2015; Kitching and Rouse 2020; McKelvie et al. 2020)
finding: Experienced entrepreneurs paid less attention to predictive information (Dew et al. 2009). Critics: effectuation lacks stated boundary conditions and testable predictions (Arend et al. 2015). Much evidence is cross-sectional questionnaires with one respondent per firm (McKelvie et al. 2020). A review of 101 articles found many ignored social structure objections (Kitching and Rouse 2020).
numbers: Systematic review counts 680 journal articles, 2001-2024 (Salajegheh et al. 2025). No pooled effect size.
limits: No head-to-head test of effectuation vs planning on the page. Secondary source.
agent_relevance: The emergent side of the debate has weak causal evidence. Do not build the agent on 'effectual' claims without a direct test on our own tasks.

source: Wikipedia: Business plan
finding: Page contains no empirical research on whether plans improve outcomes. It says costs are often underestimated and revenues overestimated, and mentions reference class forecasting as a fix.
numbers: None. The page flags itself as needing citations.
limits: Null result: the common reference page has no evidence. Evidence must come from entrepreneurship journals.
agent_relevance: Planning fallacy applies to plans: an agent's own time and cost estimates should be corrected with reference-class data from past runs.

source: Backlund and Petersson (2025) Vending-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Term Coherence of Autonomous Agents
finding: LLM agents run a simulated vending business over long horizons. Success is uneven. Every model had runs that derailed. Failures did not line up with the context window filling.
numbers: Mean final net worth over 5 runs each: Claude 3.5 Sonnet $2,217.93 (min $476.00); o3-mini $906.86 (min $369.05); human baseline $844.05 (single 5-hour run); Gemini 1.5 Pro $594.02; GPT-4o mini $582.33. Units sold min 0 for several models. Over 20M tokens per run.
quote: all models have runs that derail
limits: Human baseline is one run. High variance across runs. Early models, so absolute levels are dated.
agent_relevance: Even a good plan-and-act agent loses coherence over long horizons. S9 should check realized actions against the intended plan and trigger a reset on drift.

source: Hu et al. (2026) EcoGym: Evaluating LLMs for Long-Horizon Plan-and-Execute in Interactive Economies
finding: Eleven LLMs, three economic environments (Vending, Freelance, Operation). No model wins all three. Gaps come from two separable skills: strategic prioritization and execution efficiency.
numbers: Operation task: top model chose scale (643 items at quality 0.566) over runner-up's refinement (326 items at 0.762). Human experts (n=3, 15 min of practice, 45 min per episode) averaged DAU 1,404, which Claude-Sonnet-4.5 beat. Thinking mode lifted Gemini-3-Flash DAU from 1194 to 1396. Longer context (k=32 to 1024) gave no consistent gain.
limits: Human baseline restricted to one environment and 3 people. Relative scores. Trials: 5 runs for Vending, 3 for others.
agent_relevance: Plan quality and execution are separable. Weakness in either hurts. Score them separately to learn which one to fix.

source: Hu et al. (2026) EcoGym: memory and complexity ablations
finding: Memory modules help but not universally, and the best type depends on model and task. A bigger option space did not help the stronger model.
numbers: Gemini-3-Pro Vending-style scores: none 11282, working 13679, symbolic 15567, episodic 18939, Mem0 15406. Gemini-3-Flash: none 5676, working 10099. Complexity (Vending, N=8/16/37 items): Flash 3512 to 5676 (rises); Pro 14090 to 11272 (falls).
limits: Two models only. Single table, means with large SD in Table 4.
agent_relevance: Adding structure is not uniformly good. Match the scaffold to the model and test it, in line with our rule to add nothing without measurement.

source: Dai et al. (2026) Can LLMs Be CEOs? CEO-Bench
finding: Five models, 13 scenarios, four advisors with conflicting advice. Plan validity is easy; calibrating boldness is hard. Common failure is under-reallocation (not bold enough for the state). Other failures: single-advisor capture, history inconsistency. Deeper engagement with conflict went with less decisive plans.
numbers: Overall: Gemma-4-27B 73.86; GPT-OSS-20B 71.90; Qwen-Plus 67.17; Claude-3.5-Haiku 65.82; Nemotron-9B 63.87. Valid plans 13/13, 13/13, 12/13, 11/13, 11/13. Boldness scores 58 to 70. Plan validity 79 to 93. Temperature 0.2, one run per scenario.
limits: One run per scenario. LLM-based grading. Small, older models. The McKinsey claim (more than 50% capital reallocation creates more value, 1,600 firms) is quoted from other work, not tested.
agent_relevance: Intended plans tend to be too timid. A rule that checks plan boldness against stated state is a better test than a validity check.

source: Yang et al. (2026) EnterpriseBench
finding: Nine agent methods, four backbones, three interactive business settings (Consulting, Beer Game, Enterprise Digital Twin). No method is best everywhere and rankings flip with the backbone. Self-Refine and Reflexion fell below plain CoT on Consulting.
numbers: Consulting score: GEPA 8.28 (DeepSeek-V3), DC 8.08 (GPT-4.1). Beer Game cost: Discussion 1.94e4 best on DeepSeek-V3 but much worse on GPT-4.1. Human-LLM grading agreement r=0.71 (20 cases); r=0.887 with 85.0% within one point on 500 transcripts.
limits: Rubric-based LLM judging. Backbone-method interaction makes any single ranking unstable.
agent_relevance: Iterative self-correction alone did not help. Supports our rule that reflection needs an external check, and that scaffold gains must be re-tested per model.

source: Ovezmyradov (2025/2026) AI Playing Business Games: Benchmarking LLMs on Managerial Decision-Making in Dynamic Simulations
finding: Five chat LLMs run a 12-month retail simulation. Gemini led. ChatGPT worst, then Grok. Weaker models showed volatile pricing and reacted late. Several models crossed a point of no return in months 4 to 8 where sales fell to zero and never recovered.
numbers: Gemini Pro ROA 10.84 vs others negative (-0.3 to -6.76). Sales forecast error (MAPE) 88 to 121 for non-Gemini models. Best human player among a few acquaintances: net income $938,000 on revenue $5,023,300. Point of no return: Gemini Flash period 8; others period 4 or 5.
limits: Single run per model, free chat interfaces, one simulation. Table is garbled in text extraction. Human comparison is anecdotal. Author states results compare long-term deliberate strategy against reacting to latest data.
agent_relevance: Reactive-only agents spiral after a shock. A stored plan with explicit revision triggers would have a place; test it.

source: Prasad et al. (2024) ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
finding: Compares a reactive executor (ReAct), a fixed plan-then-execute scheme, and adaptive plan-only-when-stuck decomposition. Plan-and-Execute was no better than ReAct on ALFWorld and worse on WebShop. Adaptive decomposition beat both on all three tasks. Closest LLM analogue of deliberate vs emergent vs mixed.
numbers: ALFWorld test success: ReAct 43.3, Plan-and-Execute 43.3, Reflexion 57.5, ADaPT 71.6. WebShop: ReAct 32.0, Plan-and-Execute 17.0, LATS 38.0, ADaPT 44.0. TextCraft: ReAct 19.0, Plan-and-Execute 27.0, Reflexion 32.0, ADaPT 52.0. Gains up to 28.3, 27, 33 points. GPT-3.5 executor.
limits: GPT-3.5-class models, text environments. Gain depends on executor capability and depth limit dmax (3 or 4).
agent_relevance: Fixed up-front plan can lose to reactive action; plan only when the executor fails. A direct design hint for when to invoke a planning operator.

source: Xu et al. (2023) ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations
finding: Plan everything first, then call tools (plan-first), compared with observation-dependent step-by-step ReAct. Plan-first used fewer tokens and matched or beat accuracy, and was more robust when tools failed.
numbers: Average over six benchmarks: 64% fewer tokens, +4.4 points accuracy. On one curated set: +8 points accuracy, 43% fewer tokens. Under forced tool failure on HotpotQA: ReAct accuracy 40.8 to 0 (change -40.8); ReWOO 42.4 to 13.2 (change -29.2). Tokens 9795 vs 1986 per query; cost per 1k queries $21.29 vs $3.97.
limits: gpt-3.5-turbo. Tool-failure test is artificial (every tool returns 'No evidence found'). Plans are fixed so they cannot adapt to surprises.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence to b17: up-front plans win on efficiency and some robustness. Task type decides, so treat plan-vs-react as a router choice.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
finding: Autoregressive LLMs alone do poorly at planning and self-verification. Pairing an LLM that proposes with an external verifier raises success a lot, except on obfuscated tasks.
numbers: GPT-4 autonomous: about 12% of generated plans were executable and goal-reaching. With verifier back-prompting (up to 15 rounds): Blocks World 82%, Logistics 70%, obfuscated Mystery Blocks World about 10%. TravelPlanner best prompting strategies: 0.7% (GPT-3.5-Turbo).
limits: Position paper. Numbers are taken from earlier papers. Older models; newer reasoning models may differ.
agent_relevance: Supports external code checking of plans. A model-written plan is only as good as the verifier that rejects bad ones.

source: Chen et al. (2026) Toward an Organizational Science of Multi-Agent LLM Systems (IMACS)
finding: A contextual-bandit router picks a collaboration protocol per task. It beats every fixed protocol, including Plan-and-Execute, in a controlled study. Fixed Plan-and-Execute is the weakest in aggregate. Best accountability placement flips across model families.
numbers: Router 0.708 vs best fixed (MoA) 0.669; oracle 0.754; recovers 45% of oracle headroom; routing accuracy 82%. Plan-Execute fixed 0.550 (0.157 below router). Context-free bandit 0.628.
limits: The headline result uses a simulated latent oracle with noise (sigma 0.03), not only real model outputs. At N=10 per cell on HotpotQA, many cells equal 1.00.
agent_relevance: No fixed process wins across tasks. Choosing the protocol per task from cheap features is a measured improvement over any single fixed scheme.

source: Mintzberg (1994) The Rise and Fall of Strategic Planning (as summarized in Wikipedia)
finding: Planning coordinates and measures progress but happens around strategy formation, not inside it. Strategy formation is a creative act of synthesis. Plans mainly communicate intentions, coordinate, and win outside support. Planning done far from the front line may not help.
numbers: None.
limits: Conceptual argument. The empirical meta-analyses (b04, b06) mostly find small positive links between planning and performance, which is not the strong form of this claim.
agent_relevance: Keep planning as a coordination and checking device; place synthesis where the model works from observations.

source: Miller and Cardinal (1994) Strategic planning and firm performance: a synthesis of more than two decades of research
finding: Wide-known meta-analytic synthesis that found planning is positively related to performance on average, with moderators in the study design (for example measure of performance, and whether the sample was published). Details not verified this session.
numbers: Not verified (publisher 403; Semantic Scholar had no abstract).
limits: Recorded from memory of the literature. Included so the next pass knows to open it.
agent_relevance: Candidate source for how effect size changes with study quality.

source: Camuffo, Cordova, Gambardella and Spina (2020) A scientific approach to entrepreneurial decision making: evidence from a randomized control trial
finding: Randomized trial of Italian startups trained to treat strategy as hypotheses to test. Reported that the trained group made more and earlier pivots and did better. Publisher PDF returned 403, so not verified.
numbers: Not verified this session. Sample reported elsewhere as about 116 startups.
limits: Not opened. Treatment is training in testing, so it does not isolate plan vs emergent.
agent_relevance: The cleanest causal test in this area. Open it first in a later pass.

source: Koning, Hasan and Chatterji (2022) Experimentation and start-up performance: evidence from A/B testing
finding: Large observational study of startups using an A/B testing platform. Reported better performance with experimentation, mainly through more variants tried and through stopping poor ideas. Publisher PDF returned 403, so not verified.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Evidence for the learning loop: more cheap tests and drops of bad ideas.

source: Search coverage note: classic strategy meta-analyses
finding: Boyd (1991), Schwenk and Shrader (1993), Miller and Cardinal (1994), Brews and Hunt (1999), Rudd et al. (2008), Gruber (2007), Burke et al. (2010) and Lange et al. (2007) could not be opened. Publisher pages gave 403, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar search were rate limited, WebSearch budget was exhausted.
numbers: None.
limits: This is a gap, not a result. The next pass should open these via an open repository.
agent_relevance: Do not cite effect sizes for planning-performance from this file. Only direction (small positive, context-dependent) is supported by b04 and b05.
